newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia retailers see better Christmas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia retailers see better Christmas.

text.p: Australian retailers Woolworths Ltd and Coles Myer Ltd said on Thursday there are good signs emerging for the 1996 Christmas trade, and both expect if trends continue to be able to do better than in 1995.
Woolworths group managing director Reg Clairs told Reuters that strong trading days on Monday and Tuesday of this week had demonstrated a modest beginning to the Christmas period.
"Last week was not outstanding, it was reasonable but I would have liked to have seen it just a little better, but Monday and Tuesday were strong days," he said.

"I cannot get much more up to date than that, other than to say if you summed it all up, you would say, yes, Christmas has started, modestly, but it has started," he said, adding the pickup had come a day or two behind last year.
Asked if he expected Woolworths to trade above last Christmas, Clairs said: "Yes, I do."
"The stock has been ordered and the promotional programme has been put in place to trade above last year," he said.

"To tell you what percentage we are going to trade above last year would be difficult to predict but we have taken a cautiously optimistic approach in ordering our stock ... on the basis that we will out-trade last Christmas," he said.
Debra Stirling, general manager of public affairs at Coles Meyer said the company's view of Christmas was "cautiously optimistic".
"There are some signs of improvement," she said.
Stirling said customers were "grading up" the value of their purchases, compared to the tendency in a recession to buy bottom of the range products.
"And what this indicates is that there is a certain element of consumer confidence out there," she said.
"If the current trends continue then we will have a better Christmas than last year," she said, although adding it had been a difficult year for retailers and there was some time to go.

Both retailers welcomed Wednesday's surprise 0.5 percent official interest rate by the Reserve Bank of Australia although they said it would have been more helpful for this Christmas if it had come earlier.
"The eleventh of December, it is all over," Clairs said.
"(It is) six weeks since the last one and that has not really bitten yet, but all of this will deliver value in 1997," he said.
Stirling said there was no doubt the cut would have been more helpful if it had come earlier "but every little bit helps".
